sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dedicated Offshore Software Engineering and Maintenance Hub

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Agreement (2009, as amended)
Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Agreement (1962, as amended)
Luxembourg–France Double Taxation Agreement (1958, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), implementing Directive (EU) 2018/843; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the practical operation of the RBE; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of passport of each UBO, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport authority of country of nationality or residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement) for each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source of wealth statement for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relation bank of the applicant or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract or certificate of good conduct for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent judicial or police authority of country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for countries party to the Hague Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF) lists, CSSF administrative sanctions, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions List, and national political exposed person (PEP) databases. For the target ODC risk tier, enhanced due diligence is not automatically required, but negative news and adverse-media screening, as well as continuing transaction monitoring, must be performed under Law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers portal – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible via https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed corporate names must be submitted in French, German, or English. Non-Latin script names require a transliteration into the Roman alphabet. The legal form suffix 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' is mandatory. A French rendering is preferred for filing and publication consistency.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Terms requiring prior ministerial, CSSF, or other regulator approval: 'Banque', 'Bank', 'Assurance', 'Insurance', 'Fonds', 'Fund', 'Trust', 'Bourse', 'Pension'
Terms implying sovereign or state sponsorship: 'Luxembourg', 'État', 'National', 'Royal', 'Gouvernemental'
Words contrary to public order or public morality
Names identical or confusingly similar to existing RCS registrations or protected trademarks
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant or a Luxembourg-licensed lawyer may file a written administrative appeal with the Registrar within 15 days of notification, providing the rejection reference, legal arguments, and a revised compliant name. If the administrative appeal is unsuccessful, the applicant may bring an action before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal de l'arrondissement) within one month of the final refusal, with legal representation by an Avocat. Name reservation extensions are not guaranteed and are granted by the Registrar only on showing of good cause.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office may be used for correspondence and registered-address purposes, but the RCS registration requires a Luxembourg registered office and the company must maintain day-to-day administrative and management substance in Luxembourg. For an Offshore Development Center under ISIC 6202, a fully virtual-only address is likely to be treated as insufficient tax residence and substance evidence; a co-working or committed office lease is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for a standard-risk ODC, quantified at approximately 15% under routine administrative supervision. The likelihood rises to approximately 30% if RBE filings are inconsistent, unusual payment flows are observed, or VAT refund applications are made.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation and availability request at the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
Notarized articles of association and execution of the incorporation deed for a SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial fee schedule and prevailing market benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS electronic filing and publication in the Recueil électronique des sociétés
Certified translation of foreign corporate and UBO documents into French, German, or English
AML/KYC UBO due diligence package, PEP/sanctions screening, and negative-media screening
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for standard-risk ODC

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Initial UBO register filing with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
Registered office address agreement and mail-forwarding for the first 12 months
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg registered-agent or co-working service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk ISIC 6202 office substance package

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 19 August 2016 and the Law of 10 August 2016; SARL provisions at Articles 710-1 to 710-24; Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the craft, commercial and industrial professions; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); electronic filing coordinated through the Luxembourg notary via the LBR e-portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation containing the Articles of Association (Statuts), registered with the RCS and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations) within one month of registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The SARL must maintain a subscribed share capital of at least EUR 12,000, divided into registered shares with a minimum par value of EUR 1. At incorporation, at least 20% of each cash share (minimum EUR 2,400 in aggregate) must be paid up into a blocked bank account (compte de blocage) at a Luxembourg credit institution; such funds must remain blocked until RCS registration. Contributions in kind must be fully transferred at incorporation and supported by a report of an independent réviseur d'entreprises agréé. No statutory escrow deposit beyond the bank blocking requirement applies.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The articles of association of the company having been executed before the notary, the entire share capital of EUR 12,000, divided into 1,000 registered shares of EUR 12 each, is approved and fully subscribed by the sole shareholder. (2) The registered office is fixed at 14, Boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg, and the notary is instructed to complete all filings at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register and RESA. (3) [NAME] is appointed sole Manager (Gérant) for an indefinite term, with full authority to represent the company. (4) The Manager is authorized to open bank accounts, register for VAT, social security, and operating permits with the Ministry of the Economy, and to delegate as necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Clearance and Drafting of the Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS corporate name index, screened via a Luxembourg notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the Luxembourg notary to run the proposed corporate name against the RCS index and the Chambre de Commerce registers, obtain a negative name-conflict confirmation, and settle the French-language Articles of Association, corporate objects aligned to ISIC 6202, registered office clause, and share capital structure.
required_dossiers: Passport copy of each founding shareholder and the first Manager (Gérant)
Proof of residential address of each individual signatory dated within three months
Criminal record certificate (extrait du casier judiciaire, type no. 3) for the Manager
AML/KYC declaration and beneficial ownership form under the Law of 13 January 2019
Draft Articles of Association in French prepared by the notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name conflict or administrative query is raised, propose up to three alternative names and re-run the RCS search; escalate to the LBR support desk for a formal negative certificate before advancing to cost-bearing steps.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocked Capital Deposit at a Luxembourg Credit Institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Selected Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. BGL BNP Paribas, Société Générale Luxembourg, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the draft Articles of Association and the KYC file to the bank, open a blocked account (compte de blocage) in the name of the company in formation, deposit at least 20% of the subscribed cash capital, and obtain the bank's blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming that funds are reserved until RCS registration.
required_dossiers: Completed bank onboarding and AML/KYC forms
Draft Articles of Association
Source of funds and source of wealth declarations
Personal identification, tax residence, and passport copies of each subscriber
Bank blocking certificate as the deliverable of this step
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Engage the bank's compliance department for enhanced due diligence and provide source-of-wealth evidence and ultimate beneficial owner chart; if the file is still declined, select an alternative Luxembourg bank and resubmit the KYC pack.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Schedule the notarial signing appointment; the notary reads and authenticates the French-language Articles of Association; each shareholder or the duly authorized attorney-in-fact signs the deed; the bank blocking certificate and, where applicable, the contribution-in-kind report of the réviseur d'entreprises agréé are attached; the notary dates the deed and forwards the electronic file to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Bank blocking certificate evidencing paid-up capital
Final draft Articles of Association in French
Passports and proof of address of all signatories
Power of attorney (procuration) if signing by representative
Independent auditor's report for contributions in kind, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a statutory defect, execute a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) or amend the affected clauses by shareholder decision before registration; all signatures may be re-verified without restarting the capital blocking procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Electronic Filing, Registration, and Issuance of the L Number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS electronic filing interface
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary e-files the notarized incorporation deed via the LBR e-portal, pays the RCS registration fee (EUR 19) and electronic filing fee, the RCS registers the company and issues the RCS identification number (L number); the Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) is subsequently obtained through the LBR LEI service.
required_dossiers: Notarized French deed of incorporation in official scanned form
Articles of Association
Bank blocking certificate
RBE beneficial ownership registration confirmation
RCS and LBR fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the filing for formal errors, the notary resubmits corrected annexes within the eight-day statutory cure period; a refusal may be appealed to the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement) within one month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA Publication and Post-Incorporation Tax and Social Security Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); RESA publication via LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Publish the incorporation deed in the RESA electronic compendium within one month of RCS registration; file the VAT commencement declaration (Form 645) with AEDT to obtain the TVA number; register the company as an employer with CCSS; confirm the corporate income tax file with ACD, and retain the RCS extract and statutes as standing evidence for bank and client onboarding.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized Articles of Association
Valid identification of the Manager
Company bank account details
Registered office lease or proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT number issuance is delayed, request a provisional common identification number (matricule) from AEDT and escalate by formal written notice after 15 days; any RESA publication defect is cured by immediate re-filing to preserve third-party effectiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: General Business Establishment Permit and Municipal License Application
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement, filed through the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) via Guichet.lu; Commune de Luxembourg for municipal consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic application (Form A-02) on Guichet.lu, attaching the RCS extract, Articles of Association, and the Manager's professional credentials; obtain the autorisation d'établissement and the municipal acknowledgment before commencing payroll and client operations; no sector-specific license applies to ISIC 6202 software development services.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Articles of Association
Manager's valid ID and criminal record certificate (type no. 3)
Professional competence evidence (diploma or at least three years relevant experience)
Lease agreement or registered office proof
Guichet.lu submission confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the authorities query the dossier, complete the requested evidence within 10 business days; a final refusal may be appealed to the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months, and business operations must await permit issuance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie - Direction de l'autorisation d'établissement), coordinated through the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) and Guichet.lu; Commune de Luxembourg for municipal building and business approval
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 regulating access to the craft, commercial and industrial professions; no sector-specific or financial sector license applies to the ISIC 6202 offshore software development activity.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - low environmental risk office and software development operations: exempt from a full EIA study; simplified registration and notification under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment (implementing EU Directive 2011/92/EU), processed together with the commune's building and occupancy permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater only, compliant with municipal sewerage standards implementing EU Directive 91/271/EEC; no VOC or fine particulate emissions from software development activity; compliance with EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and the Luxembourg Law of 9 December 1997 on packaging waste; electronic and office hazardous waste must be collected by certified operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Occupancy and fire safety clearance from the municipal fire and rescue service (Service d'incendie et de secours - SIS) obtained through the building permit procedure; electrical installation conformity certificate; structural load verification per the amended Luxembourg Building Code; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering office ergonomics, emergency exits, fire drills, and workplace welfare standards of the amended Labour Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) — Luxembourg Inland Revenue (impotsdirects.public.lu) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) (aedt.public.lu) for VAT and registration duties; Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu (myguichet.lu) as the single e-government filing portal
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: (1) File notarized articles of incorporation with the RCS through the notary/MyGuichet.lu and obtain the RCS extract registering the corporate identity; (2) submit the AEDT electronic VAT registration application, yielding a VAT number in format LU + 8 digits, attaching the RCS extract, articles of association, EU/EEA seat certificate of the foreign parent, and identity documents for managers and ultimate beneficial owners; (3) direct tax registration with ACD is generated ex officio in the form of the corporate matricule/TIN; (4) file the ultimate beneficial owner (RBE) return within 30 days; (5) a business license (autorisation d'établissement) is not required for ISIC 6202 offshore software development activities — the ODC is an unregulated commercial activity
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; an LU SARL is an opaque, tax-resident legal entity (registered seat or effective management in Luxembourg) subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax on worldwide income; no passthrough eligibility; foreign PE income qualifies for treaty-based exemption with progression and the participation exemption shields qualifying dividends and capital gains; no sub-national tax distinction in Luxembourg (unitary national system)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box regime: classification is statutory. Available elections: (1) VAT single-unit (assujetti unique) grouping for VAT; (2) fiscal integration (intégration fiscale under Art. 164bis LIR) for 95%+ owned Luxembourg subsidiaries; (3) treaty-based branch/PE exemption election (exemption-with-progression); (4) Nexus-compliant IP Box election (Art. 50ter LIR) granting an 80% exemption of net qualifying IP income, including copyrightable computer software and databases relevant to the ODC; (5) ATAD hybrid-mismatch notification/neutrality elections; the SCSp partnership transparency election is available only for alternative vehicle structures

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax — TVA (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), harmonized with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC and implemented by the Luxembourg VAT Code (Code de la TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 (Luxembourg-established small business annual exemption threshold, excluding VAT); non-resident suppliers have no threshold — any taxable supply triggers Luxembourg VAT registration unless the B2B reverse charge, EU OSS/IOSS regime, or the EUR 10,000 EU-wide cross-border distance-sale threshold applies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory B2B e-invoicing or real-time fiscal clearance as of 2025; no tax-authority clearance or digital stamping (fiscal cachet) exists; PEPPOL-BIS electronic invoicing is mandatory only for suppliers to central public authorities; the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) package, effective March 2025, will mandate structured e-invoicing and transaction reporting for LU VAT-registered entities in phases from 2030, but there is currently no continuous transaction control (CTC) system

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: 0% export VAT under Art. 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Code where title passes to a non-EU purchaser and the goods are physically dispatched from Luxembourg to a destination outside the EU, with transport evidence and an export declaration filed with customs. Services (ISIC 6202 ODC scope): software engineering, maintenance, hosting and digital services rendered by the SARL to customers established outside the EU fall outside Luxembourg VAT (place-of-supply B2B destination rule under Arts. 17(2) and 24 of the VAT Code), producing an effective 0% outcome; services to EU B2B customers are reverse-charged in the customer's member state. Zero-rating eligibility requires the recipient to be non-established in Luxembourg and, for digital services, effective use and enjoyment to occur outside Luxembourg
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD - Single Administrative Document or electronic export declaration lodged via Luxembourg Customs e-Douane/ECS module)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical dispatch to a non-EU destination
Inward Remittance Certificate (bank SWIFT/MT103 or correspondent credit confirmation evidencing export proceeds received by the LU SARL within the agreed payment term)
Signed contract/statement of work and itemized invoices for the offshore software development and maintenance services
Proof of the client's non-resident status (EU VIES validation certificate, foreign VAT registration certificate, or tax residence certificate)
Delivery evidence (acceptance reports, sign-off tickets, IT access logs, and remote-delivery records)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and ACD require complete export and cross-border service files during audit; insufficient substantiation triggers reassessment at 17% VAT plus 0.8% monthly late-payment interest; intentionally fraudulent zero-rating claims attract administrative penalties of up to 100% of the evaded tax, criminal fines of up to EUR 50,000, and imprisonment of up to two years; the normal five-year limitation period is extended to ten years for fraud; retrospective disallowance of input VAT credit and joint and several liability of directors and the controlling foreign parent apply

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the Eurosystem under the authority of the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) serves as the prudential and AML/CFT supervisor of credit institutions in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is freely convertible, and Luxembourg maintains a fully liberalized capital and current account regime pursuant to Articles 63-66 TFEU and Council Directive 88/361/EEC. No prior exchange-control authorization is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, intercompany service payments, or profit repatriation by a Luxembourg SARL. External account and current account transactions are unrestricted, and no differentiated surrender or buyback regime applies to residents. The only material frictions to profit remittance are fiscal rather than FX-related: Luxembourg dividend withholding tax at 15%, reducible to 5% or 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or applicable double tax treaties, together with ordinary corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax borne before distribution. Cross-border payments trigger BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting, but that obligation lies on the reporting credit institution, not on the company, and no permission or restriction is attached to such reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg and the euro area impose no surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory deadline for the repatriation of export proceeds. Export receivables may be retained in foreign currency indefinitely, converted at commercial rates, or netted internally subject to transfer-pricing arm's-length principles. For a low-risk cost-plus ODC whose functional currency is EUR, best treasury practice is to match invoicing and disbursement currencies, convert foreign receipts within the contractual payment cycle, and periodically revalue foreign-exchange balances under IFRS or LuxGAAP to recognize foreign-exchange gains or losses; non-compliance with such practice is a fiscal and audit issue, not a BCL violation.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (day-to-day EUR disbursements, salary payments, SEPA, and VAT payments)
Capital Escrow Account for the statutory EUR 12,000 SARL share capital deposit and subsequent corporate operational account
Operational Account and FX/cross-currency hedging master account
Capital Escrow Account and operational account with trade-finance support
Operational Account for payroll and contractor disbursements
Operational Account and high-value cross-border clearing rail

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium for low-value operational disbursements; Low for statutory escrow and BCL-statistical-reporting duties. Under PSD2, an electronic money institution (EMI) licensed in an EEA member state may passport payment accounts, IBANs, and money-remittance services into Luxembourg, so offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Wise Business, Payoneer, Revolut Business) can technically provide EUR IBANs and SWIFT rails. The decisive legal constraints are: (1) a bank account at a BCL-reporting credit institution is required to evidence the SARL capital deposit and to facilitate the notarial deed; (2) EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot issue escrow confirmations acceptable to a Luxembourg notary or the RCSL; (3) cross-border receipts routed exclusively through EMIs may remain outside the bank's balance-of-payments reporting loop and create a BCL statistical compliance gap; and (4) business-operations clauses of several tier-1 banks prohibit primary payroll and social-security flows through EMIs. The blueprint therefore authorizes EMI rails only as a secondary egress for sub-EUR 50,000 contractor payments, with the main treasury ledger and all statutory capital, payroll, and tax flows maintained at a BCL-reporting credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not universally require physical presence of directors for account opening, but standard tier-1 bank policies mandate an in-person interview of at least one director or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) at the Luxembourg branch, before a Luxembourg notary, or at the bank's relationship office in another EEA jurisdiction before the account is activated. Remote video-KYC onboarding is available today but is typically conditioned on: (i) a certified copy of the articles of association against the RCSL extract; (ii) the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) registration extract; (iii) notarially authenticated UBO identification documents; and (iv) a positive name-screen of all signatories. Consequently, the compliance blueprint must reserve a director visit to Luxembourg for the interview signature, corporate signatory confirmation, and production of original source-of-funds documents; a remote-opening alternative should be pre-negotiated only with fintech EMIs and must not be relied upon for the primary account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-EEA cross-shareholder chain: a parent or UBO located outside the EEA with no prior relationship with the Luxembourg bank triggers enhanced due diligence and possible account-opening refusal on source-of-wealth grounds.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified corporate group chart, certified passports of all natural shareholders, the RBE declaration, bank statements of the direct parent covering the source of funds for the capital deposit, a source-of-wealth file comprising salary slips, audited financial statements of the funding entity, tax returns, and the signed ODC service agreement demonstrating a genuine commercial purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Uneconomic capital or lack of substance: a statutory EUR 12,000 deposit for a company planning to book multi-million-euro revenue is treated as a classic shell indicator and triggers an automatic financial-crime review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Three-year business plan, forecast P&L and cash-flow statement, the client contract or master services agreement, lease agreement for Luxembourg premises, payroll and social-security registrations, and transfer-pricing documentation showing the ODC's functional profile and arm's-length margin.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO or trade counterparty appearing on a sanctions list or negative-news database, including the EU consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, or Interpol notices, causing the bank to freeze funds or reject the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance-screener exemption file containing a detailed explanation of the detected partial name match, passport copy with date of birth, proof of jurisdiction of residence, a board resolution appointing the UBO, and an external AML legal opinion confirming that no sanctions-targeted interest exists in the SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Discrepancy between the declared activity (ISIC 6202 IT consulting) and expected large cross-border credits from affiliates, which may be perceived as round-tripping or hidden cash pooling.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoicing register for the ODC's development services, time-tracking and acceptance reports produced under the commercial contract, intercompany cost-allocation file, and transfer-pricing analysis confirming that the cross-border payments constitute arm's-length service remuneration rather than tax-motivated flows.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The capital injection from the parent or investor must be executed by SWIFT MT103 single-customer credit transfer (or MT202 COV for an interbank cover arrangement) to the SARL's escrow account at a BCL-reporting bank, settled in EUR via TARGET2. Field 50 must bear the funding shareholder's account; Field 70 (Remittance Information) must read 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION / LU_SARL <RCSL registration number>' to enable purpose-of-code classification; the bank also requires the underlying notarial draft deed and a capital deposit instruction letter signed by the shareholder. Verification steps: (i) sanctions and name screening of the remitter; (ii) KYC check on the source of funds; (iii) BCL balance-of-payments coding as direct investment in equity; and (iv) notarization and filing of the deed with the RCSL before the escrow restriction is lifted. No BCL exchange-control approval is required. For non-EUR injections, the bank will convert at its corporate rate, and the inward transaction must be pre-declared for transfer-pricing consistency with the parent.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Credit Transfer (ISO 20022 pain.001) is the primary rail for EUR disbursements within the EEA, covering salaries, social security, suppliers, and intra-group fees, with SEPA Instant for sub-EUR 100,000 urgent payments and TARGET2 for high-value settlements. Non-EEA and non-EUR payments use SWIFT MT103 for credits to beneficiary accounts and MT202 COV for cover payments; each payment carries a purpose code (e.g., SUPP for supplier payment, SALA for salary, INTC for intercompany charge) in Field 70 while the bank runs EU, OFAC, and UN sanctions screens and BCL statistical classification. Commercial letters of credit (documentary credits under ICC UCP 600) are available through the trade-finance desks of BIL, BNP Paribas Luxembourg, and Société Générale Luxembourg for procurement of hardware or licensed infrastructure where the supplier requires an LC; standby LCs are not required for the ODC's ordinary software-engineering fee flows. The bank account may not be used as a pass-through of third-party funds, and no cross-border payment exceeding EUR 200,000 should be issued without a board-approved cash-flow forecast and, where relevant, the CRS/FATCA remittance report.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable plain-vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF) executed under an ISDA Master Agreement and the 1998 FX and Currency Options Definitions, as amended.
FX swaps (swap-in/swap-out) for short-term liquidity conversion between EUR and the ODC's receivable currencies, with tenors not exceeding 12 months.
Cross-currency swaps converting long-term intercompany debt (e.g., USD shareholder loans) into EUR exposure, matched by the SARL's assets and approved by the board.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permitted exclusively for hedging genuine commercial exposure in restricted non-convertible currencies (e.g., INR, KRW, RUB), with an EEA-licensed investment firm counterparty when a deliverable forward is unavailable.

Cancellable FX option or zero-cost collar structures, allowed only with an investment-grade counterparty, a signed board hedging policy, and full integration into the ODC's transfer-pricing documentation.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of RCS registered details (confirmation annuelle RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due every year during the calendar month of the company's RCS registration anniversary; confirmation is performed electronically through the LBR online portal.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A missed deadline produces a LBR reminder notice; two consecutive years of non-confirmation expose the SARL to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) after a formal summons, together with fines for registered managers up to EUR 25,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (comptes annuels) filing with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, filing must be completed by 31 July. Shareholders' approval of the annual accounts must occur within six months of the year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing renders the registered managers liable to court fines ranging from EUR 750 to EUR 25,000; failure to file for two consecutive financial years may trigger administrative deletion from the RCS, judicial publication of the default, and civil liability for consequential damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner confirmation and one-month UBO updating notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), maintained by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation must be performed during the same RCS annual-confirmation month; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership requires an RBE update within one month from the effective date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: False, incomplete, or late UBO filings attract criminal fines up to EUR 125,000; repeated non-compliance may result in a court-ordered update, publication of the offence, and negative regulatory risk reporting by banks and notaries.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax (CIT) and net wealth tax (NWT) return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filing due by 30 June following the relevant tax year; extension to 31 December is routinely available when submitted electronically by a tax-admitted professional through the MyGuichet platform.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts penalties up to EUR 10,000 and default interest at 0.6% per month on unpaid taxes; the tax authorities may proceed by official assessment (imposition d'office) on unreported income, with additional criminal tax fines in cases of fraudulent omission.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint a certified independent auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) if it exceeds at least two of the following thresholds at the balance-sheet date for the two last consecutive financial years: balance sheet total above EUR 4.4 million; net turnover above EUR 8.8 million; average workforce above 50 full-time employees. Audit is also compulsorily required for public-interest entities, regulated financial-sector undertakings, securitisation vehicles, and any company whose articles or shareholders' resolution so provide.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (LU GAAP) under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on annual and consolidated accounts; EU-endorsed IFRS applies only to listed public entities and is optional for consolidated accounts; individual SARL accounts are prepared under the Luxembourg normative chart of accounts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The RBE data is confirmed annually together with the RCS data in the LBR electronic portal; the registered manager certifies that the recorded beneficial-owner identities are current and accurate. Any shareholding transfer or change in control is a triggering event requiring RBE remediation within one month of the effective date, and the same transfer must be entered without delay in the Register of Members. Evidence of the annual confirmation must be retained and made available to the CSSF, notaries, banks, and tax inspectors on request.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 1,200 – 2,500 USD per annum for a Luxembourg registered address plus corporate-agent compliance services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 8,000 – 25,000 USD per annum for a small-to-mid-sized SARL requiring a statutory audit, depending on group structure, transfer-pricing documentation, and consolidated reporting requirements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate: 17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge on CIT + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income, effective rate approx. 5%); Notional Interest Deduction; participation exemption (100% for dividends and capital gains meeting substance thresholds); investment tax credit for qualifying software and hardware; no standalone statutory tax holiday.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory carryforward time limit; restrictions may apply upon change of ownership under anti-abuse rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via eTVA through MyGuichet.lu
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within six months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year companies, the regular deadline is 30 June of the following year. Extensions are discretionary and must be requested in writing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal identification: SARL name, registered office, matricule number (RCS/RNET), VAT number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Provide the Luxembourg VAT and matricule identifiers; attach the certificate of liability if the SARL is managed by a foreign appointed manager.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit-and-loss data under LUX GAAP or IFRS, including turnover, salary expenses, depreciation and bad debt provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg SARL, issue audited or reviewed financial statements per Luxembourg statutory rules; no consolidation is allowed for CIT purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses and tax adjustments: excess interest, fines, penalties, gifts, and any hidden profit distribution deducted in the accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the ODC derives services from related parties, add-back charges not supported by valid invoices or lacking economic substance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption deduction: 100% of qualifying dividend income from Luxembourg or foreign subsidiaries.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the SARL holds at least 10% (or an acquisition cost above EUR 1.2 million) and is subject to tax equivalent; provide subsidiary TRC and substance evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Municipal business tax base adjustment and rate of the commune where the Luxembourg establishment is registered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The municipal business tax is assessed on the PE or place of effective management; a foreign owner cannot elect a lower-rate commune without actual premises and staff there.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after adjustments, loss carryforwards, and non-deductible provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Luxembourg SARL owned by a non-resident, taxable income remains the Luxembourg legal entity's profit; transfer pricing adjustments must be included for remote software development services.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an ex-officio assessment (taxation d'office), a late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid CIT, and administrative fine up to EUR 2,500 plus a 10% surcharge (minimum EUR 50) on the legally due tax for late filing or understatement.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg dividend withholding tax; reduced to 0% where the participation exemption conditions are satisfied (holding >=10% and other substance requirements).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and a Form 720/721 request to the Luxembourg direct tax administration. After prior approval, the Luxembourg payer may apply the reduced treaty rate at source. If the statutory 15% has already been withheld, a refund claim (demande en restitution) must be filed with the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes within 12 months of the withholding date, attaching TRC and evidence of beneficial ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax; Interest: 0% domestic withholding tax for standard corporate interest payments, with no DTA limitation in most cases; certain interest paid to resident individuals from bonds may be subject to a 15% withholding tax under domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 (group consolidated turnover) and cross-border controlled transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 1,000,000 trigger the obligation to maintain a Local File and, where subject to Group reporting, a Master File; CbCR applies at EUR 750,000,000. Contemporaneous OECD-compliant TP documentation is recommended for any related-party transaction of the ODC.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg is not an Economic Substance Regulation jurisdiction, but the tax administration enforces economic substance principles under the GAAR (Article 6 AStL? CTL), the Luxembourg participation exemption, and ATAD. The ODC must have real staff, physical office premises, and commercial control in Luxembourg. Absent such substance, treaty benefits and domestic exemptions can be denied and the income may be reallocated to the beneficial owner/source State.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful misreporting of ODC revenues, fabrication of invoices to inflate costs, concealment of intercompany service charges, or deliberate false statements in Form 100.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of unpaid CIT plus 10% administrative surcharge and monthly late payment interest; criminal fine up to EUR 125,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years (Article 59 LIR).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director may be held jointly and severally for evaded corporate tax if personally involved; civil restitution, travel bans, and disqualification from managing Luxembourg companies; criminal imprisonment for fraudulent intent.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging the offshore dev center a mark-up below arm's length, providing services without substantiated cost‑plus benchmarking, or routing R&D payments to an offshore associate without accurate TP documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: TP adjustment under the OECD Guidelines; additional tax assessment up to 10% penalty on the understated profit; secondary dividend reclassification; interest for late payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for reckless advice or false declarations; assets can be attached in execution of tax liabilities; a travel ban may be issued when substantial unpaid taxes are being dismantled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Luxembourg SARL has no employees, no operational premises, no board decision‑making effect in Luxembourg, and serves merely as an invoicing shell for the offshore software services.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and the participation exemption; reattribution of profits to the owner/beneficiary; court‑ordered striking‑off from the Luxembourg register; penalty up to 10% of the additional assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell SARL can be sued in civil restitution for damage caused to the State and third parties; prohibition from acting as director; travel ban imposed if non‑compliant with tax summons.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the beneficial ownership statement in the Luxembourg RBE register, lack of proper know‑your‑client due diligence for foreign software development clients, or cash transactions exceeding statutory thresholds without disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004; enforcement by the Public Prosecutor; underlying tax fraud penalties may also apply.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors exposed to personal fines up to EUR 1,000,000; prohibition from exercising managerial positions; imprisonment for repeat debt non‑payment and money‑laundering offenders.
